title: [Refurb] HP EliteDesk 800 G4 Micro Intel i5 8500T 8GB RAM 256GB SSD $160.65 ($156.87 eBay Plus) Delivered @ ACT eBay
body:
Deal: [Refurb] HP EliteDesk 800 G4 Micro Intel i5 8500T 8GB RAM 256GB SSD $160.65 ($156.87 eBay Plus) Delivered @ ACT eBay

[Averell] Is it good storing security cameras records?
Thanks
[Commodore64] 256gb will be tight but usable with pruning
[myr] Mines a lenovo with the same chip, happily runs proxmox & frigate with a dozen cameras, i5-8500T sits 15%ish doing igpu reencoding, or practically idle if your cameras natively encode how you want to record.
I'd suggest a refurbed enterprise 2.5" or something reasonably robust for the storage though.
[dan0909] your Lenovo is much better though, same with Dell. HP works if it works longterm, reliability is not same as Lenovo Thinkcenter and Dell Optiplex.
[Averell] How about power consumption?
I'm thinking of also running Home Assistant on that. Its capability is not my concern, but how much power it consumes is.
Thanks
[OldSchoolHarry] For HA, you can save power consumption by going with a Thin Client instead.
For example, Dell Wyse 5070 runs on Pentium Silver j5005 which whilst having plenty of grunt for HA, only has TDP of 10w compared to 35w with i5 8500T.
[OzSikh] Does it come with the power supply included?
[BROKENKEYBOARD] I'd assume so but the only thing on ebay I see is:
Very Good - Refurbished: The item shows minimal wear. It is fully functional and has been professionally refurbished, tested, inspected and cleaned to very good condition by the eBay seller or a third party. The item includes original or new accessories and may come in generic packaging. See the seller's listing for full details.
Their main website does specify it:
https://www.australiancomputertraders.com.au/hp-elitedesk-80…
https://www.australiancomputertraders.com.au/lenovo-thinkcen…
[geekcohen] Exactly, I have a Lenovo similar running PiHole without a problem.
[Mechz] It's actually overkill as I am running mine on an iGel D220 thin client. But good value either way.
[Sfh1975] Overkill. You can run a pihole on almost anything, e.g. some Asus routers with custom fw. A newish RPi will run HA and Adguard no problem.
[PainToad] I hope you're not seriously wasting one of these solely for running PiHole.
[vos0003] I have pihole running on my 2013 raspberry pi 1 with 512mb ram 🤣
[OldSchoolHarry] Same. And before that I had it running on pi zero w and never had any issues.
[ReaperX22] Presumably you'd run proxmox with a pihole via an lxc and run other crap on it.
For a dedicated pihole yeah this is overkill.
My old Intel 2820 nuc is pretty solid as a dedicated pihole to be fair, though. And even that's probably slightly overkill for it but it's nice not to wait forever for it to update too! (though atm this nuc is in storage..)
[Mechz] I run DietPi OS. Has a LOT of software options out of the box so you don't have to search and install individually.
[Sfh1975] @Mechz: I used to run that on a RPi 4 but it was getting tired. The arrs can be quite hungry sometimes.
[HeyPapito] Extremely overkill for a PiHole setup. You can run this on a Pi Zero for under $30
[preemo] Any good deals on Raspberry Pis? I find they are crazy expensive now.
[tman2020] As others have said, overkill just for pi-hole. But great little box for proxmox containers and VMs running pi-hole, home assistant, proxy managers, wireguard etc.
[PainToad] With Switch recomps starting to happen, this could be a good little device for native Switch games.
[Zex94] How would this be for potentially self hosting an LLM?
[myr] you may as well run ollama on your desktop for better performance if its just for education.
I tested gemma3 for image categorisation at about 60sec to analyse an image on my i5-8500T w 32gb ram, which is good enough for my bin reminder in home assistant. Text reponses from some of the smaller qwen models ran fast enough but so much lower quality I wouldnt use them.
[BalticBishop] Self hosting an online LLM is what it's good for. Just run a chatgpt instance 24/7.
[bargaino] LLM is possible, I suppose.
e.g. You could run Gemma 4 edge model, use it for voice-control home automation.
16GB and 11th gen+ would be easier though.
Don't need a brain the size of a planet to "hey Gemma, turn off the lights".
[freelife] I have the G6 i7 and it chokes on even small local LLMs. I just use OpenRouter using Qwen3.8-Flash which is ridiculously cheap but very capable. Less than 1 cent for most tasks. I switch to GPT-6.1-Sol for bigger jobs
[allewell] Great price/performance balance. 8th gen CPU, when Intel realised they couldn't be lazy any more and had to ship meaningful improvements.
[TaurusHead] 8GB RAM is a bit low, 16GB is the least nowadays
[OZKap] This definitely won't play GTA6 when it comes out.
[TaurusHead] I know, and I was just saying in general, no judgements against this price
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] It's a valid comment 1-2 years ago but everything has changed since the shortage.
[OZKap] In the recommend tab was the same (with nothing ) for ~$100 shipped, 100+ available https://www.ebay.com.au/itm/256696508455
NO Power Adapter, NO CPU, NO RAM, NO HDD
Is there actually a market for a mini case + motherboard?
[Mechz] No RAM or SSD I could understand, but what the hell did they do with the CPU?
[bargaino] Desoldered it i guess. You have to admire the effort.
[BargainBuddy] Check the model spec. Some mini pcs comes with sata. Iv have seen lenovos with pcie slot for low end gpus
[dan0909] Lenovo Thinkcenter and Dell Optiplex are more reliable. Our of 16 HPs we bought for shop/office in 2022 and 2023 only 7 remain the rest had various issues over time and we replaced. Our Dell Optiplex machines are still going from 2019.
[the1doood] I had similar experiences with HP too. Latest one was flagged by Windows about disk about to die.
[SkyeMG] hmm good to know.
ima miss out on this fomo for this one hehe
[jedimaster] I have a G2 running 24/7 as a plex server for 3 years in a row. Great little machine
[dibbz] re: media pc usage, only the display port does 4k @ 60hz, the hdmi is 24 or 30hz, you would need an active adapter from the dp to hdmi if you wish for that.
[melbstheburn] Would this be good for home usage i.e browsing, word, occasional YouTube? Or anything worthwhile under $300?
[Mechz] Fine as long as you don't have too many tabs open at once.
[melbstheburn] Would this be good for home usage i.e browsing, word, occasional YouTube? Or anything worthwhile under $300? Any help would be greatly appreciated
[OzSikh] this would definitely be perfect for your use case
[Jackjcca] What about running heavy tasks? any recommendation? What should i look for? multiple tabs + gpt + claude maybe?
[OzSikh] multiple tabs + gpt + claude - No issues
[Jackjcca] @OzSikh: would you recommend this or https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/977881 ?
Don't mind going for the kill, and having extra space to run stuff, just don't want to keep spending $$ and having ot upgrade
[OzSikh] @Jackjcca: Lenovo M90q has Double the Processing Threads (12 vs. 6), 16GB RAM Out of the Box, Two Generations Newer (Hardware Longevity). Go for Lenovo, you won't regret
[cooldude123] would this be useful for something like Blue Iris or Frigate?
[BargainBuddy] Intel 8th gen will work with Frigate detection. Frigate uses the iGPU through OpenVINO, which is supported from 6th gen onward.
An 11th gen is faster, so it can handle more cameras. Mine runs 7 cameras with detection without issues.
If the price is a bit higher, go for a 10th or 11th gen. For Home Assistant alone, either is more than enough.
[OZKap] Presumably your phone cost more than $160
[wetsandwich] Honestly, i5 8th gen and 8gb ram for that price is very very grim, even with the shortages etc..
My work will pretty much be paying to throw away 10th gen minis in a few weeks (and no, unfortunately I can't get any held for anyone)
[BargainBuddy] I can help you with the disposal free of charge. Dm me mate.
[safrane] Yeah it's pretty insane how 8th gen is still at this price, I recall it was about the same price 2 years ago. Even EoL devices aren't immune from inflation and the RAMpocalypse.
